verifications.claim: Artemis 2 reentry and splashdown is on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'reenter Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026'; R2: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego on April 10'; R3: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R6: 'return to Earth tonight, April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm reentry and splashdown on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: Coverage of Artemis 2 reentry and splashdown begins around 6:30 p.m. EDT (2230 GMT) on NASA's YouTube channel, NASA+, and the NASA app.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:30 p.m.: NASA+ coverage begins' ... 'streamed live on NASA+, the NASA app, and its YouTube channel'; R3: '6:25 p.m. ... Coverage will continue'; R6: 'beginning at 6:30 p.m. EDT (2230 GMT)' ... 'NASA+, the space agency's free streaming service. The feed ... on NASA's YouTube channel'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state coverage starts around 6:30 p.m. EDT on NASA+, YouTube, and app.

verifications.claim: Orion capsule will splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'; R2: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All sources consistently confirm splashdown location off San Diego in Pacific Ocean.

verifications.claim: Orion capsule will splash down around 8:07 p.m. EDT (5 p.m. PDT/0007 GMT April 11).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources exactly match time as 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT / 0007 GMT April 11.

verifications.claim: Orion capsule will hit the atmosphere at ~24,000 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'rip through the atmosphere at roughly 24,000 mph'; R5: 'speeds reaching 25,000 mph'; R6: 'plunge through Earth's atmosphere at about 24,000 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly support ~24,000 mph entry speed; minor variation to 25,000 not contradictory.

verifications.claim: Orion capsule reentry generates a fireball that is crucial to test the heat shield.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'agitating the air around the capsule into a fireball' ... 'NASA will use a new, more direct reentry technique, after the heat shield ... unexpectedly chipped'; R6: 'fiery 13-minute plunge ... heat shield ... critical test on Artemis 2'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe fireball during reentry and emphasize heat shield testing in that context.

verifications.claim: According to officials, Southern Californians will likely not be able to see the re-entry or splashdown in person.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Southern Californians likely won’t be able to see reentry or splashdown in person, NASA officials said. ... "The path we’re coming in, I don’t expect it to be visible for folks in California," Artemis II Lead Flight Director Jeff Radigan said'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from NASA official matches claim exactly.

verifications.claim: Artemis 2 mission returns Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Artemis II crew'; R2: 'Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and ... Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and ... Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: All listed sources name the exact four astronauts returning on Artemis 2.

verifications.claim: Artemis 2 mission astronauts complete a 10-day trip around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day milestone mission to orbit the moon'; R2: 'After 10 days'; R3: 'approximate 10-day mission around the Moon'; R6: '10-day trip to the moon'
